A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PDGF B-subunit gene is up-regulated in hyperoxia and that this precedes the proliferating response in the microvessels and alveolar epithelium.
PDGF B-chain is the major ligand expressed by cells at the lung periphery during the early proliferative response in hyperoxia, whereas PDGF A-chain is expressed by cells at a later stage.
PDGF B-chain and beta-receptor are the major growth factor components involved in the remodeling response in the lung to hyperoxia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PDGF receptor and its ligands are expressed at high levels in the peripheral lung of rats breathing high oxygen levels.
PDGF receptor subunit expression is regulated differentially in hyperoxia, and this is associated with the proliferation of specific cell populations.
the PDGF B chain is the main growth factor that operates while the lung remodel in hyperoxia.
